Non-payment of Dividends: Dividends are noncumulative; if the Board of Directors does not declare a dividend for any period, the company has no obligation to pay it, and holders lose the right to receive it.  Interest Rate Risk: The dividend rate resets after May 15, 2031, based on the five-year treasury rate, meaning future dividend payments could be lower if treasury rates fall.

Comparable offerings from other major banks, such as JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo, often feature similar fixed-to-floating rate structures and noncumulative dividends to qualify for Tier 1 capital treatment under Basel III regulations.
